name: AlgoLaser DIY Kit MK3 15W
tagline: Balanced 15W module of the MK3: engraving and 3 mm cutting on a 400 × 400 mm frame for $309
tldr: The DIY Kit MK3 15W is the middle tier and the one AlgoLaser calls 'Everyday Maker's Choice': the 400 × 400 mm frame, AlgoOS touchscreen and focus stick of the MK3 with a 15W diode for faster engraving and routine 3 mm cutting. At $309 it costs only $50 more than the 8W. AlgoLaser publishes no cutting figure for this module, and no independent review exists yet.
mainObjective: All-round engraving and light cutting on a mid-size bed at a budget price

priceRange.note: Official AlgoLaser store, Oct 2026: $309 machine only, $509 Basic kit (honeycomb, RR2 rotary roller, riser kit, air pump)

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood 3 mm (routine), thicker with several passes
cannot: Bare metal (no infrared module listed for the MK3)
Enclosed use without the optional enclosure

pros: Only $50 more than the entry module for clearly faster engraving
Handles routine 3 mm basswood and plywood cuts with air assist
Full MK3 package: touchscreen, focus stick and 400 × 400 mm frame for $309
cons: No published cutting thickness or optical power test for this module
Air assist is not included with the machine-only version
Open frame with no enclosure in the box
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 15W tier of the DIY Kit MK3, the one most buyers should compare first. Against the 8W it adds speed and cutting margin for $50; against the 20W it saves $150, which pays for air assist and a honeycomb. Take the 20W only if cutting wood is your main job.
proTips: Pair the 15W with air assist before cutting anything: it keeps edges clean and the lens free of smoke. Do batches of coasters from the touchscreen's stored projects, and move to LightBurn for photo work. Expect 3 mm in one or two passes and plan more passes beyond that.

faq.question: How thick can the DIY Kit MK3 15W cut?
faq.answer: AlgoLaser does not publish a figure for the 15W. Plan on 3 mm basswood or plywood as routine, about 6–9 min for a 10 × 10 cm square in our benchmark, and several passes for 5–6 mm. AlgoLaser's 12 mm one-pass claim applies to the 20W only.

faq.question: 15W or 20W?
faq.answer: The 20W costs $459 with a free air pump against $309 for the 15W on AlgoLaser's store (October 2026). The 20W cuts faster and AlgoLaser rates it for 12 mm wood in one pass. For mostly engraving with some 3 mm cutting, the 15W plus a $69 air assist is the better buy.

faq.question: Does the 15W need a computer?
faq.answer: Not for simple jobs: the AlgoOS touchscreen engraves text, sketches and over 400 stored projects on its own. For photos, vector files and precise layouts, connect LightBurn, LaserGRBL or the AlgoLaser app.

moduleSystem.headline: Three diode modules on the same MK3 frame
moduleSystem.description: The DIY Kit MK3 is sold with an 8W, 15W or 20W diode module on the same 400 × 400 mm frame and touchscreen. The power is chosen at purchase; modules fit the same head mount, one at a time.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 15W is the sensible default of the MK3 range: close to the 8W in price, much faster in use, and enough for routine 3 mm cutting. With a touchscreen and a 400 × 400 mm frame for $309, it undercuts most open-frame rivals of similar size.
editorialDepth.limitations: AlgoLaser gives no verified cutting figure for this module, air assist costs extra on the machine-only version, and the open frame needs ventilation and eye protection. No independent review has tested it yet.

standoutFeatures.title: The balanced tier
standoutFeatures.body: AlgoLaser positions the 15W as its everyday module: faster engraving than the 8W and routine 3 mm cuts for only $50 more.

standoutFeatures.title: Offline touchscreen
standoutFeatures.body: Text, sketches and stored projects run straight from the AlgoOS screen, so batches of coasters do not need a computer.
